themes_detail.label: Pool/Beach Facility Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Beach/pool/sauna complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 1100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting a sudden facility closure, contamination, or service disruption affecting Greenwich Village residents during peak summer season.
evidence: 3 beach/pool/sauna complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Timing coincides with summer recreation season when demand is highest
No recent news coverage of facility issues—suggests story is breaking now
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to determine which facility is affected and why complaints spiked—closure? water quality issue? staffing shortfall?
Interview residents about access to summer recreation; explore equity angle if facility serves low-income community

themes_detail.label: Underground Infrastructure Collapse Risk
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints exploded to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)—indicating potential subsurface infrastructure failure threatening pedestrian safety across the district.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72—highest anomaly)
Curb condition also spiked: 12 complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (540% increase, z-score 7.98)
Converging signals suggest systemic street/subsurface deterioration, not isolated incidents
Community Board budget requests show 'Clean catch basins' as repeated unfunded ask—DEP maintenance backlog may be relevant
reporting_angles: FOIA request to DEP for subsurface inspection records and maintenance work orders in CD 102 over past 6 months
Walk affected blocks with visual documentation; identify which streets show worst deterioration
Interview residents about sinkholes, water main breaks, or other infrastructure failures they've witnessed

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping & Abandoned Vehicles Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping jumped 217% to 23 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO (vs. 7.2 weekly average), and abandoned vehicles surged 348% to 14 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO (vs. 3.1 average)—convergent spikes suggesting organized dumping activity or sanitation service breakdown in the district.
evidence: Illegal dumping: 23 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 7.2 weekly baseline (217% spike, z-score 4.15)
Abandoned vehicles: 14 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly baseline (348% spike, z-score 3.88)
Two separate but related problems spiking simultaneously suggests common root cause
Community Board budget requests repeatedly ask for 'more sanitation trucks and equipment'—chronic capacity issue
reporting_angles: Map the specific locations of dumping and abandoned vehicle complaints to identify hotspot neighborhoods
Investigate whether DSNY enforcement has been reduced or redeployed; check for service cuts or budget changes
Interview community members about whether they've seen organized dumping or illegal chop shops operating

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials & Environmental Contamination
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked 500% to 3 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO (vs. 0.5 weekly average, z-score: 3.54), and illegal posting complaints jumped 700% to 3 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO—suggesting potential environmental contamination, hazard signage removal, or industrial activity in a gentrifying commercial district.
evidence: Hazardous materials: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
Illegal posting: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 3.77)
Combined signals suggest either new hazard sources or removal of warning signage
SoHo/Spring Street area has active ULURP (246 Spring Street) with ongoing development—construction-related contamination risk
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP and DOHMH to determine what hazardous materials were reported and from which locations
Cross-reference with DOB building permits (1556 filings in last 90 days, mostly alterations)—did construction trigger hazmat complaints?
Investigate whether hazard remediation signage is being removed illegally at development sites

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Mandate or Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints spiked 1100% to 3 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO (vs. 0.2 weekly average, z-score: 6.35)—suggesting either a citywide water conservation order, supply disruption, or public awareness campaign that residents are reporting as a problem.
evidence: Water conservation complaints: 3 three weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Isolated spike with no recent news coverage suggests timing may predate major water system announcement
Heat/hot water complaints also high across district (1260 total in 90 days)—possible correlation with water management changes
reporting_angles: Check DEP announcements or NYC.gov for water conservation orders or supply advisories from 3+ weeks ago
Verify whether spike corresponds to seasonal maintenance, a specific water main break, or citywide policy
